symptom: `mxcli git merge` merged a model with another Mendix version's `mx merge` when the project's exact version was not installed: the merge commit was written by that engine and nothing warned.
cause: realMxMerge and realMxDiff called docker.ResolveMxForVersion, which treats the version as a preference: it takes an mx on PATH first, then the newest installed one, then any cached download, and returns no error when none matches.
fix: mergeMxLookup resolves mx once per run and checks docker.MxBinaryVersion against the project's _ProductVersion with docker.SameMendixRelease; another release, or an mx whose version cannot be told, is an error, so the runner fails before exec and the existing abort path restores the tree. --mxbuild-path is the override (warns once), the same rule marketplace package's checkMxVersion applies.
insight: ResolveMxForVersion's 'any version will do' fallbacks are right for read-only checks and wrong for anything that writes the model; every writer (new, marketplace package, fix hashes, now git merge) has had to add its own exact-version check. Grep for ResolveMxForVersion callers that write before trusting the resolver.
test: cmd/mxcli/gitmerge_mx_version_test.go (another version refused and aborted; unknown version refused; --mxbuild-path runs the engine with one warning; control: with the check stubbed out all three fail)
